edges.description: The chimeric protein retains CIC's DNA-binding domain while carrying a DUX4-derived activation domain, so CIC target genes are no longer repressed.

The fusion acts with the P300/CBP transcriptional co-activators to repress MHC class I antigen presentation, and the dependency runs through the fusion: in the murine model, switching it off restores presentation. Whether the repression is a direct output of the fusion or runs through its target programme is untested - the source reports no occupancy experiment at these loci, and both of its manipulations collapse the whole programme at once - so this edge is drawn from the lesion for want of a demonstrated intermediate, not because independence has been shown.
edges.target: MHC Class I Antigen Presentation Suppression

edges.description: Relief of repression at PEA3 subfamily targets, and direct activation by the fusion, raise their expression.
The transcriptional programme the fusion drives includes cell cycle progression genes, and produces a rapidly growing undifferentiated tumour.
The proliferating tumour presents as the deep soft tissue mass that brings the patient to attention.
More than half of patients develop metastases, at a median of 10.5 months in one series. The steps between the proliferative phenotype and dissemination are not established for this entity.
The tumour is treated on Ewing sarcoma protocols because it looks like Ewing sarcoma, but its biology is different and its outcome is worse.
edges.target: Poor Response to Ewing Sarcoma Chemotherapy

edges.description: Without MHC class I on the tumour cell there is nothing for a cytotoxic T cell to recognise, and the microenvironment stays depleted of them.
edges.source: MHC Class I Antigen Presentation Suppression

edges.description: The fusion alone generates the tumour in this system, which is what makes it evidence that the fusion causes the proliferative phenotype rather than accompanying it.
edges.limitations: The recipient cell is a mouse embryonic mesenchymal cell chosen for the experiment, not an identified human cell of origin, so the model shows the fusion is sufficient in a permissive mouse cell and says nothing about which human cell the tumour arises from. The fusion is introduced by transduction from a cDNA rather than arising as a translocation, so expression is not under the endogenous promoter. The tumours are mouse tumours, and the markers derived from them were validated separately on human cases. The recipient cell matters: the same fusion introduced into bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells produced neither the downstream expression changes nor growth, which the authors read as the fusion's function being cell context-dependent at least in part.
edges.source: CIC-DUX4 ex vivo mouse model (embryonic mesenchymal cells)

edges.description: The system the suppression was characterised in, and the one that establishes it depends on the fusion: withdrawing doxycycline, or inhibiting P300/CBP, restores presentation.
edges.limitations: The MHC class I genes measured are the mouse ones, H2d1, H2k1 and mouse beta-2 microglobulin, not HLA. The fusion is expressed from an inducible transgene rather than from a translocated endogenous locus, so its level is set by doxycycline - which is also why the model's own switch-off experiment has no counterpart in a patient-derived line. The human confirmation quoted on the node is a different manipulation, P300/CBP inhibition, and it was reported only in combination with interferon gamma, where the mouse system showed recovery without it. That difference is unexplained in the source and is itself a candidate species difference rather than a readout artefact.
edges.source: Doxycycline-inducible CIC::DUX4 chimeric mouse and the imChCDS line derived from it

edges.description: Syngeneic transplants of the line into immunocompetent hosts are where the cold microenvironment and its reversal were observed.
edges.limitations: A mouse immune system against a mouse tumour expressing a transgenic fusion protein, which could itself contribute antigenicity that a human tumour would not present. The cohorts are small and the regression experiments change two things at once - cell cycle arrest and antigen presentation - so the model does not separate the immune contribution from the proliferative one.

nodes.description: A rapidly proliferating tumour of small to medium round to ovoid cells showing no line of differentiation, with prominent nucleoli, a high mitotic count and areas of necrosis. In the mouse model, the transcriptional programme downstream of the fusion includes the cell cycle gene Ccnd2, and silencing the fusion or Ccnd2 inhibits tumour growth, which ties the proliferative phenotype to the fusion rather than to an unrelated secondary event.

biological_processes: positive regulation of cell population proliferation

evidence.reference_title: High prevalence of CIC fusion with double-homeobox (DUX4) transcription factors in EWSR1-negative undifferentiated small blue round cell sarcomas.
evidence.snippet: Microscopically, tumors displayed a primitive, round to oval cell morphology with prominent nucleoli, high mitotic count, and areas of necrosis.

evidence.reference_title: CIC-DUX4 Induces Small Round Cell Sarcomas Distinct from Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Recipient mice transplanted with eMC-expressing CIC-DUX4 rapidly developed an aggressive, undifferentiated sarcoma composed of small round to short spindle cells.

evidence.reference_title: CIC-DUX4 Induces Small Round Cell Sarcomas Distinct from Ewing Sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Gene-expression profiles of CDS and eMC revealed upregulation of CIC-DUX4 downstream genes such as PEA3 family genes, Ccnd2, Crh, and Zic1

evidence.reference_title: Sarcomas With CIC-rearrangements Are a Distinct Pathologic Entity With Aggressive Outcome: A Clinicopathologic and Molecular Study of 115 Cases.
evidence.snippet: A CIC-DUX4 fusion was detected in 57% of cases, with either DUX4 on 4q35 (35%) or on 10q26 in 25 (22%) cases.

evidence.reference_title: High prevalence of CIC fusion with double-homeobox (DUX4) transcription factors in EWSR1-negative undifferentiated small blue round cell sarcomas.
evidence.snippet: RACE, RT-PCR, and/or long-range DNA PCR performed in two cases with frozen material showed that CIC was fused to copies of the DUX4 gene on either 4q35 or 10q26.3.

nodes.description: A somatic rearrangement of CIC on 19q13, most often fusing it to a copy of the double homeobox gene DUX4 on 4q35 or 10q26.3, through a t(4;19)(q35;q13) or t(10;19)(q26;q13) translocation. CIC encodes the human homologue of Drosophila capicua, a high mobility group box transcription factor. In the fusion most of the CIC protein is retained, including its DNA-binding HMG box, and the C-terminal fragment of DUX4 supplies a transcriptional activation domain. This is a change in kind rather than in degree: the product is a chimeric transcription factor with an activity the wild-type repressor does not have, which is why the molecular function here is marked GAIN_OF_FUNCTION rather than INCREASED.

evidence.reference_title: Fusion between CIC and DUX4 up-regulates PEA3 family genes in Ewing-like sarcomas with t(4;19)(q35;q13) translocation.
evidence.snippet: CIC, a human homolog of Drosophila capicua which encodes a high mobility group box transcription factor, is fused to a double homeodomain gene DUX4 as a result of a recurrent chromosomal translocation t(4;19)(q35;q13).

evidence.reference_title: Fusion between CIC and DUX4 up-regulates PEA3 family genes in Ewing-like sarcomas with t(4;19)(q35;q13) translocation.
evidence.snippet: CIC-DUX4 exhibits a transforming potential for NIH 3T3 fibroblasts, and as a consequence of fusion with a C-terminal fragment of DUX4, CIC acquires an enhanced transcriptional activity, suggesting that expression of its downstream targets might be deregulated.

evidence.reference_title: High prevalence of CIC fusion with double-homeobox (DUX4) transcription factors in EWSR1-negative undifferentiated small blue round cell sarcomas.
evidence.snippet: CIC rearrangements by FISH were detected in 15/22 (68%), while none showed FUS abnormalities.

nodes.description: Mouse embryonic mesenchymal cells were transduced with human CIC-DUX4 cDNA and transplanted into recipient mice, which developed an aggressive undifferentiated sarcoma of small round to short spindle cells. The model reproduces the fusion's downstream programme, including the PEA3 family genes seen in human tumours and the cell cycle gene Ccnd2, and it was the source of CCND2 and MUC5AC as markers separating this tumour from Ewing sarcoma.
nodes.id: CIC-DUX4 ex vivo mouse model (embryonic mesenchymal cells)

nodes.description: The usual presentation is a deep-seated soft tissue mass. In the 115-patient cohort 86 per cent of tumours were in soft tissue, mostly deep, divided about equally between trunk and extremity, with 12 per cent visceral and 3 per cent in bone. This distribution is one of the practical differences from Ewing sarcoma, which commonly arises in bone.

evidence.reference_title: Sarcomas With CIC-rearrangements Are a Distinct Pathologic Entity With Aggressive Outcome: A Clinicopathologic and Molecular Study of 115 Cases.
evidence.snippet: Most tumors occurred in the soft tissue (86%), predominantly deep-seated and equally divided among trunk and extremity, followed by visceral locations (12%) and rarely in the bone (3%).

evidence.reference_title: CIC-rearranged Sarcomas: A Study of 20 Cases and Comparisons With Ewing Sarcomas.
evidence.snippet: Although none of the CIC-rearranged sarcomas arose in the bone, 40% of the Ewing sarcomas primarily affected the skeleton.

nodes.description: A chimeric mouse carrying a doxycycline-inducible CIC::DUX4 transgene, and a dox-tunable cell line established from its tumours. The fusion alone is enough to produce soft tissue tumours, and the tumours resemble human CIC sarcoma by histology and by expression profile - the authors report the chimeric tumours correlating with tumours from the Kitra-SRS and NCC-CDS-X1 human lines and with patient samples. What this model adds over the existing ex vivo and xenograft models is an intact immune system: the line is tumorigenic in immunocompetent as well as immunodeficient hosts, which is what makes the antigen-presentation and T cell work possible, and the dox switch makes the fusion's contribution reversible on demand.
nodes.id: Doxycycline-inducible CIC::DUX4 chimeric mouse and the imChCDS line derived from it

evidence.reference_title: Modeling CIC::DUX4 sarcoma reveals oncogene-mediated MHCI-dependent immune evasion.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that CIC::DUX4 expression alone is sufficient to drive tumorigenesis in permissive lineages of soft connective tissues.

evidence.reference_title: Modeling CIC::DUX4 sarcoma reveals oncogene-mediated MHCI-dependent immune evasion.
evidence.snippet: Spearman correlation analysis revealed that the gene expression profiles of the chimeric tumors closely resembled those of tumors derived from Kitra and X1 cell lines, as well as CDS patient tumor samples.

nodes.description: Most patients receive Ewing sarcoma regimens, because the tumour was classified with Ewing sarcoma until 2020 and because no regimen has been developed for it. The evidence that this works is weak. Durable responses were infrequent in a national series, with a median response duration of 2.1 months and one durable complete response to VDC/IE, and a review for radiologists describes the entity as responding poorly to standard Ewing sarcoma treatment. No prospective trial has compared regimens in this entity.

evidence.reference_title: Systemic treatments and outcomes in CIC-rearranged Sarcoma: A national multi-centre clinicopathological series and literature review.
evidence.snippet: One durable complete response of metastatic disease to VDC/IE chemotherapy was seen. Responses to pazopanib (n = 1) and pembrolizumab (n = 1) were not seen.

evidence.reference_title: Undifferentiated Small Round Cell Sarcomas: Radiologic-Pathologic Correlation for the Updated WHO Classification Fifth Edition (2020).
evidence.snippet: Radiologic recognition of CIC-rearranged sarcomas enables oncologists to anticipate their aggressive nature and poor response to standard ES treatments, which may necessitate more intensive initial surgical interventions.

nodes.description: Few infiltrating T cells, which is what the suppression of antigen presentation buys the tumour. In the syngeneic model the state is reversible: restoring MHC class I is accompanied by T cells arriving within days. The node stops there and does not assert that the cold microenvironment is what sustains tumour growth. Switching the fusion off arrests the cell cycle as well as restoring presentation, and in immunodeficient hosts the same withdrawal makes established tumours regress with no T cells available at all - so regression cannot be attributed to the immune arm.

animal_models.description: Syngeneic transplants of the line into immunocompetent hosts are where the cold microenvironment and its reversal were observed.
animal_models.name: Doxycycline-inducible CIC::DUX4 chimeric mouse and the imChCDS line derived from it

evidence.reference_title: Modeling CIC::DUX4 sarcoma reveals oncogene-mediated MHCI-dependent immune evasion.
evidence.snippet: imChCDS cells develop CDS-like “cold” tumors in immunocompetent mice.

evidence.reference_title: Modeling CIC::DUX4 sarcoma reveals oncogene-mediated MHCI-dependent immune evasion.
evidence.snippet: While T cells in the DoxON group were predominantly CD4 +, dox withdrawal induced a significant shift toward CD8 + cytotoxic T cells

evidence.reference_title: Modeling CIC::DUX4 sarcoma reveals oncogene-mediated MHCI-dependent immune evasion.
evidence.snippet: Genetical inactivation of CIC::DUX4 or pharmacological inhibition of P300/CBP induces cancer cell cycle arrest, restores MHCI expression, and triggers robust anti-tumor immune responses, thereby transforming the immunologically "cold" CDS microenvironment into a "hot" one and driving tumor regression.

nodes.description: Wild-type CIC is a transcriptional repressor whose effectors include the PEA3 subfamily ETS transcription factor ETV4. The fusion replaces that repressive output with activation at the same targets. The relief of repression is recorded here as a decrease in repressor activity; the resulting rise in PEA3 factor expression is the next node.

evidence.reference_title: Inactivation of Capicua drives cancer metastasis.
evidence.snippet: Inactivation of CIC relieves repression of its effector ETV4, driving ETV4-mediated upregulation of MMP24, which is necessary and sufficient for metastasis.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular and therapeutic advancements in Capicua (CIC)-rearranged sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: These early studies collectively suggest that CIC cooperates with SIN3/HDAC and the mSWI/SNF repressor complexes to transcriptionally silence target genes in mammalian systems.

molecular_functions: DNA-binding transcription repressor activity, RNA polymerase II-specific

nodes.description: Presentation of endogenous peptide on MHC class I is repressed, which is how the tumour escapes recognition. The repression is transcriptional and runs through the fusion together with the P300/CBP co-activators. In the murine system, surface presentation recovers both when the fusion is switched off and when P300/CBP is inhibited, and transcript levels of the MHC class I genes recover when the fusion is switched off; transcript-level recovery under P300/CBP inhibition is reported for the human lines rather than the mouse ones. It is not a mouse-only effect - treating human CIC::DUX4 sarcoma cell lines with a P300/CBP inhibitor alongside interferon gamma restores presentation almost completely in one line and partially in the other. DUX4 has been reported to suppress MHC class I antigen presentation in other settings, which is the background this result sits against.
nodes.id: MHC Class I Antigen Presentation Suppression

evidence.snippet: RT-qPCR analysis further confirmed CIC::DUX4-dependent repression of MHCI–related genes, including H2d1, H2k1, and β2m

evidence.reference_title: Modeling CIC::DUX4 sarcoma reveals oncogene-mediated MHCI-dependent immune evasion.
evidence.snippet: Within 48 h, combined iP300w and IFN-γ treatment almost completely restored MHCI presentation in X1 cells and partially in Kitra cells

nodes.description: Metastatic disease is common, either at presentation or during follow-up. In a national multicentre series, 7 of 18 patients had advanced disease at diagnosis, metastases developed in 55 per cent overall, and the median time to recurrence was 10.5 months. Median overall survival in those presenting with advanced disease was 12.6 months.

evidence.reference_title: Systemic treatments and outcomes in CIC-rearranged Sarcoma: A national multi-centre clinicopathological series and literature review.
evidence.snippet: In this series, CIC-rearranged sarcomas affected young adults and had a high incidence of presenting with, or developing, metastatic disease.

evidence.reference_title: Systemic treatments and outcomes in CIC-rearranged Sarcoma: A national multi-centre clinicopathological series and literature review.
evidence.snippet: In patients with advanced disease at diagnosis, median OS was 12.6 months (95% CI 5.1-20.1), 1-year OS was 57%.

nodes.description: The fusion directly binds and upregulates PEA3 subfamily ETS genes. Gene-expression analysis of the fusion identified ETV5 and ETV1 as targets and showed direct binding to, and significant upregulation of, the ETV5 promoter. ETV4, the third PEA3 member, is the one used diagnostically: strong diffuse nuclear ETV4 staining is present in CIC-rearranged tumours and essentially absent from their mimics.

evidence.reference_title: Fusion between CIC and DUX4 up-regulates PEA3 family genes in Ewing-like sarcomas with t(4;19)(q35;q13) translocation.
evidence.snippet: Gene expression analysis identified the ETS family genes, ERM/ETV5 and ETV1, as potential targets for the gene product of CIC-DUX4. Indeed, CIC-DUX4 directly binds the ERM promoter by recognizing a novel target sequence and significantly up-regulates its expression.

evidence.reference_title: ETV4 is a useful marker for the diagnosis of CIC-rearranged undifferentiated round-cell sarcomas: a study of 127 cases including mimicking lesions.
evidence.snippet: All CIC-rearranged undifferentiated round-cell sarcomas (on core needle biopsies and open biopsies) were ETV4-positive with a strong diffuse nuclear pattern.

molecular_functions: DNA-binding transcription factor activity, RNA polymerase II-specific

nodes.description: Survival is substantially worse than in Ewing sarcoma matched for age and stage, and durable responses to systemic therapy are uncommon. This is the clinical consequence that makes the distinction from Ewing sarcoma worth drawing at diagnosis rather than afterwards. The node records an outcome, not a resistance mechanism: no molecular mechanism of chemoresistance is established for this entity.
nodes.id: Poor Response to Ewing Sarcoma Chemotherapy

evidence.reference_title: Sarcomas With CIC-rearrangements Are a Distinct Pathologic Entity With Aggressive Outcome: A Clinicopathologic and Molecular Study of 115 Cases.
evidence.snippet: Clinical follow-up was available in 57 patients, with a 5-year survival of 43%, which was significantly lower than the 77% 5-year survival in the control Ewing sarcoma group (P=0.002).

evidence.reference_title: Modeling CIC::DUX4 sarcoma reveals oncogene-mediated MHCI-dependent immune evasion.
evidence.snippet: Clinically, CDS presents as a rapidly progressing disease with high metastatic potential and a strikingly poor prognosis, often exhibiting resistance to standard chemotherapy regimens adapted from Ewing sarcoma protocols

evidence.reference_title: Systemic treatments and outcomes in CIC-rearranged Sarcoma: A national multi-centre clinicopathological series and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Durable systemic therapy responses occurred infrequently with a median duration of systemic treatment response of 2.1 months.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular and therapeutic advancements in Capicua (CIC)-rearranged sarcoma.
evidence.snippet: CIC::DUX4, the proto-typical CIC fusion oncoprotein is associated with rapid clinical progression and chemotherapy resistance leading to poor clinical outcomes.
